findings.what: Hole in READ TABLE row 2. Row 2 ('twin - K2 >= +0.002: F1 = twin; F2 = K2 if d1 >= -0.001 [OK], else K1 if submitted and scored [OK], [else exp52]') is matched first, so rows 4/5, which submit K1, never run. The failing case is twin - K2 >= +0.002 with d1 <= -0.002, e.g. K2 0.952, twin 0.954. Nothing then submits K1, so F2 falls to exp52 (0.950). Yet K1 (= #35 path + inert C01; its dummy sha equals the exp57b dummy; #35 scored 0.954) is the natural insertion hedge for a twin F1 that has no insertion. The case is rare (~3-5%), but it is exactly the world where the insertion+lowrefine interaction is suspect, and it must be written down before any score (R7: no choosing the rule by the result).

findings.what: READ TABLE row 1 (K2 ERROR -> K1) does not check the error class, and the poller cannot see it: the CLI CSV has no error column, while the Kaggle API object has error_description. (a) 'Kaggle Error' (infrastructure) with the twin COMPLETE: the clean replication is to resubmit K2 v1. K1 would drop lowrefine with no evidence of harm. (b) 'Notebook Timeout' / 'Notebook Exceeded Allowed Compute' on BOTH K2 and the twin: K1 has the same GPU phase and deadlines, so it would likely fail the same way. (c) 'Notebook Threw Exception' / 'Submission CSV Not Found' / 'Scoring Error' on K2 only (twin OK): the cause is the insertion/lowrefine interaction, so K1 as written is right.
